# Prompt Modes Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

The modes a prompt is sent in, each for a different kind of work on the code and the spec.

### Shape

#### Description

There are five modes, and wherever they are listed, they are in this order.

#### Modes

- Code: changes the code, leaving the spec as it is; a subtle red
- Chain: changes the code and the spec together; purple
- Spec: changes the spec, leaving the code as it is; a subtle blue
- Ask: asks a question about the code and the spec, changing neither; a subtle green
- Freeform: passes the prompt to the agent just as it is written; grey, the theme's tertiary text colour

#### Colours

Whatever shows a mode, or something sent in it, takes the mode's colour, a tint of the [ThemeScope](../../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope)'s hue of that name, readable in both light and dark mode. Chain is Code and Spec together, so wherever it shows Code and Spec as well, both are purple: the colour midway between Code's and Spec's. A colour chosen for Code, Chain, Spec, or Ask in the theme editor, as the [ThemeScope](../../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope) says, is used in place of that mode's, Chain staying midway between Code and Spec unless it is chosen too.

#### Tasks

A prompt sent in Code, Chain, Spec, or Freeform is a task, sent as the [PromptSendingScope](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says. Tasks carry on one conversation, one at a time, and queue while the harness is working. Before one is sent, the spec is built ahead of it, as the [SpecBuildScope](../../spec-build/index.md#spec-build-scope) says. Once one finishes without error, having changed files, it adds a commit note to the [GitPanelScope](../../../ui/components/git-panel/index.md#git-panel-scope).

#### Questions

A prompt sent in Ask is a question. It runs straight away, alongside any task and any other question, and never queues, builds the spec, or adds a commit note. Questions carry on a conversation of their own, apart from the tasks', as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says.

#### Freeform

A prompt sent in Freeform is passed to the harness exactly as it was typed, with anything attached to it, and nothing else: no system prompt, no hidden anchor compiled from it, no spec built ahead of it, no slices, whatever the Slice toggle says, and no understanding file. Otherwise it is a task like any other: it queues while the harness is working, carries on the tasks' conversation, heads the message list, is saved in the prompt history, can be cancelled or resent, and adds a commit note once it finishes having changed files. It is saved in the history as a hidden anchor like any task's, recording its mode, so the queue and history hold it as they hold the others, but that anchor is never compiled, imports nothing, and has no system prompt. Its header shows the prompt as it was sent, with no hidden anchor named, and the right sidebar doesn't slide out while it runs, since it references nothing. What is sent to a running Freeform task, from Send to task, goes just as it was typed too. It is never sent to another mode, alone or in a batch.

#### System Prompts

Each mode but Freeform sends its own system prompt, from the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope). A prompt keeps the mode it was sent in while it waits in the queue.

# Harness Integration Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

Uses the one-off version of a coding harness for the selected ProjectDirectoryScope: `claude -p`, `codex exec`, or `opencode run`, whichever the user chose. Each run carries on a conversation, so the harness keeps its context between requests.

### Shape

#### Description

Should always run in auto mode.
The compiled systemPrompt of a prompt's hidden anchor is appended to the harness's own system prompt, for example with `--append-system-prompt`.
The prompt is given to the harness on its standard input, and what the harness does is streamed back as it happens. A task's run takes its prompt as a stream of messages rather than a single one, so it can be fed more while it works, as its feeding says.
Its directory, which a system prompt's HARNESS_DIRECTORY stands for, is that of the harness in use: .claude, .codex, or .opencode.

#### Harnesses

The harness in use is the one picked in the [SettingsWindowScope](../settings-window/index.md#settings-window-scope): Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, Claude Code until another is picked. It is remembered for the user, as the [UserPreferencesScope](../user-preferences/index.md#user-preferences-scope) says, not for a project. Every run the application starts goes to it, the tasks, the questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the notes and commit messages it writes, and everything else works the same whichever it is. A run already going when another is picked finishes with the harness it started with, and a conversation is only carried on by the harness it began with; the next request with another harness starts a new one.
Each harness is run its own way, streaming what it does as a line of JSON per event, which is read into the same reply, tool calls, usage, and result, whichever harness wrote it:

- Claude Code is `claude -p`, in auto mode, the system prompt given with `--append-system-prompt`, a conversation carried on with `--resume`, and a copy of one with `--fork-session`.
- Codex is `codex exec`, with `--full-auto` and `--json`, the prompt read from its standard input, a conversation carried on with `resume`.
- OpenCode is `opencode run`, with `--format json`, a conversation carried on with `--session`.

Codex and OpenCode take no system prompt of their own, so it is given ahead of the prompt, marked off from it. Neither can carry on a copy of a conversation, so a question asked while another is running starts a new conversation with them instead. The notes and commit messages are written with a small model where the harness can be told one, Claude Code's haiku, and with the harness's default model otherwise.
When the harness picked isn't installed, a run fails saying that it can't be run, as any run that can't be started does.

#### Feeding

A task's run is given its prompt as a stream of messages: Claude Code with `--input-format stream-json`, each message written as a line of JSON on the harness's standard input, which stays open for as long as the run lasts. The run's first message is the task's compiled prompt, as ever, and each message sent to the task after it, from the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope), is written as another.
A message reaches the harness when it finishes what it is doing rather than interrupting it, so a run that is mid-tool-call takes it once that call is over. The harness echoes each message back as it takes it in, with `--replay-user-messages`. A message taken in between turns is answered with a result of its own, and one taken while a turn is under way is answered within that turn, sharing its result. A result no longer ends the task on its own: the run ends with a result once every message sent has been taken in, at which point its input is closed and the task finishes, in the state of that last result. A run that is stopped closes its input straight away.
Codex's `codex exec` and OpenCode's `opencode run` read a single prompt and can't be fed more while they work, so a task running with either takes its prompt as ever and can't be sent more.
Questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the notes and commit messages each take a single prompt, as ever.

#### Images

Images attached to a prompt, as the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, are given to the harness as it takes them: to Claude Code as image content blocks, base64-encoded with their media type, in the same stream-json user message as the prompt's text, after it; to Codex with an `--image` argument per image; and to OpenCode with a `--file` argument per image. A message fed to a running Claude Code task carries its images the same way, and a Claude Code run that isn't fed more but has images is given its prompt as a stream-json message too, so the images can go with it. Codex's options end with `--` before the prompt when it is given images. Questions take images as tasks do.

#### Context

The harness keeps its context between requests instead of starting fresh each time. Tasks share one ongoing conversation, and each task sent carries it on. When the project is opened, tasks carry on the latest conversation in its history. Questions from the Ask tab share a separate conversation of their own, and when the project is opened they carry on the latest conversation among the questions saved with it. A question asked while another is running carries on a copy of that conversation, so questions running at the same time never write over each other. A conversation is only carried on in the project it began in, each open project keeping its own tasks' and questions' conversations while it is in the background, and if one can't be carried on, the next request starts a new one. Each run applies its own prompt's systemPrompt, even when it carries on a conversation begun in a different mode. The palette's file search always starts fresh.
A conversation can be left for a new one, from the chat input's New conversation button, as the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says: the next request starts a new conversation with no context, and the one left is not carried on again, not by a run of it still going, nor by the project's history. Leaving it is kept with the project, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, so a project opened after its tasks' or questions' conversation was left starts a new one too, rather than carrying on the latest conversation in its history, until a run after the reset begins one of its own. How much context a conversation holds is known from what the harness reports with each reply: everything the model was given, cached or not, and what it wrote, as of its latest reply; replies of subagents don't count.

#### Baked Prompts

[BakedSystemPromptsScope](./baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts-scope)

#### One Off Runs

[OneOffAgentRunScope](./one-off-run/index.md#one-off-agent-run-scope)

#### Catalog

[HarnessCatalogScope](./catalog/index.md#harness-catalog-scope)

#### Mode System Prompts

[ModeSystemPromptsScope](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope)
# Project Locations Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

Where in a project its spec and its code are, and which files are counted as being there.

### Shape

#### Description

A project's locations are set in the piton.config.pi of the [ProjectDirectoryScope](../project-directory/index.md#project-directory-scope), each a path relative to the project directory.

#### Locations

- the spec location is `root`, of its piton-config anchor
- the code location is `codeRoot`, of its belay-config framework
- the shape location, which mirrors the code location folder for folder, is `shapeRoot`, of its belay-config framework

#### Missing

A location missing from the config is left out of whatever would use it, or, where it can't be left out, what needs it says it couldn't be read.

#### Listing Files

The files under a folder, whether a location or the whole project directory, are every file at any depth, hidden ones included, leaving out `.git` and whatever the project's `.gitignore` files ignore. They are shown by their path relative to the project, and sorted by it.
The spec files are the .pi files under the spec location, and the source files are the files under the code location. A use can leave out more, or cap how many it takes.

# Mode System Prompts Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

The system prompt each mode sends, which tells the harness what kind of work a prompt is, and which each project can make its own.

### Shape

#### Description

Each of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) has a system prompt template. A prompt sent in a mode gives its hidden anchor a systemPrompt property, alongside its userPrompt, from that mode's template.

#### Templates

A template is Piton prose, like the prompt it is sent with, so it can reference the spec, with six placeholders, CODE_LOCATION, SPEC_LOCATION, HARNESS_DIRECTORY, SPEC_READING, PITON_FLUENCY, and UNDERSTANDING_FILE, each written after a dollar sign and inside braces like a Piton interpolation. Before the prompt is compiled, all but UNDERSTANDING_FILE are filled in: SPEC_READING first, with the spec-reading prompt, so the placeholders it holds are filled in too; then CODE_LOCATION and SPEC_LOCATION with the code location and the spec location, as the [ProjectLocationsScope](../../project-locations/index.md#project-locations-scope) says, HARNESS_DIRECTORY with the directory of the harness in use, and PITON_FLUENCY with the project's Piton fluency. Each can be moved or removed, like any other text of the template.
HARNESS_DIRECTORY is the directory the harness that runs the prompt, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, reads its agentic Markdown and reference files from, written without a leading ./: .claude for Claude Code, .opencode for OpenCode, and .codex for Codex, the directories the [NewProjectScope](../../new-project/index.md#new-project-scope) names for them.
UNDERSTANDING_FILE stands for the path, from the project directory, of the task's understanding file, and is filled in as the prompt is sent, once the task's history record is named, so a prompt sent from the queue is given its own. A question from the Ask tab has no understanding file, and UNDERSTANDING_FILE is filled in with nothing.

##### Mode

the prompt is sent in the other mode, with that mode's system

prompt, and saved in the history as a new task in that mode.

Its system prompt is Spec's, followed, on a paragraph of its own, by the code-to-spec prompt of the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope), which says that the prompt was first sent to change the code, and now the spec is to be written to describe what was built, and holds the code task's prompt, as it was typed, and its final

##### Output

the reply text after the code task's last tool call, all of it

when it made none. A code task that left no final output, having failed, been cancelled, or said nothing after its last tool call, is said to have left none. Its user prompt is the prompt as typed, as for any resend.
The new Spec task remembers the code task it was sent from, in its history record, so resending it sends it the same way, with the same prompt and final output, and its header shows, beneath the hidden anchor's name, that it was sent from Code. A Spec task sent to Code is sent with Code's system prompt alone.
A task that has been sent to the other mode no longer offers to be sent there once that has succeeded, and every task sent in Code or Spec alone keeps its button in the same place either way: once the task sent from it has finished as Done, its Send to Spec or Send to Code button is greyed out and disabled, in the latest task's header and in its heading among the previous tasks, its tooltip reading "Sent to Spec" or "Sent to Code". The batch actions neither count nor send it, though it can still be selected. While the task sent from it is waiting in the queue, building, compiling, or running, the button is disabled too, its tooltip reading "Being sent to Spec" or "Being sent to Code", so it isn't sent twice. If that task fails, is cancelled, or is left "Not recorded", as when the application closed while it ran, or a queued prompt sent from it is cancelled, the button is enabled again. A resend of the task sent from it counts the same: once any task sent from it finishes as Done, the button is disabled. Every task sent to the other mode, from Code or from Spec, says in its hidden anchor, saved before it runs and in the queue as much as in the history, which task it was sent from, by that task's hidden anchor's name, so this holds for queued prompts and for tasks restored from the history, and for as long as the task it was sent as is there. Tasks sent before this was recorded say nothing of it, and the tasks they were sent from offer to be sent again. That name is never sent to the harness. Resend is still offered either way.
A task that was itself sent from the other mode is complete: its prompt has been through both the code and the spec, so it never offers to be sent back. Its Send to Spec or Send to Code button is greyed out and disabled for good, in the latest task's header and in its heading among the previous tasks, its tooltip reading "Complete, sent here from Code" or "Complete, sent here from Spec". Being complete wins over every other state, sent, being sent, or marked done. Right-clicking it opens no menu, since it can't be marked not done, and the batch actions neither count nor send it, though it can still be selected. A resend of such a task is complete in the same way, since it remembers the task it was first sent from.
A task can also be marked as sent by hand, for a prompt whose other half was written some other way. Right-clicking its Send to Spec or Send to Code button, enabled or not, in the latest task's header or in its heading among the previous tasks, opens a small context menu there with "Mark as done", with a check icon, or, on a task marked so, "Mark as not done", with a rotating-arrow icon; one menu is open at a time, and closing it gives the focus back. Only these buttons have it, so questions, and Chain and Freeform tasks, which have none, never do. Marking it done greys out and disables its button as though it had been sent and finished, its tooltip reading "Marked as done" unless it has also been sent, and sends nothing; marking it not done enables it again, unless a task sent from it is still under way or finished as Done. Right-clicking never opens or closes the item. The mark is saved with the task in the project's data, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, in its history record, changing nothing else in it, so it is kept across restarts. A task with no record yet, left "Not recorded", is given a record holding only the mark, and still reloads as "Not recorded", marked. A task marked while it runs keeps the mark in memory until its run saves its record, which saves the mark with it, and a mark changed while that record is being saved is saved again after it. content.text:
Code tasks can no longer change the spec, and Spec tasks can no longer change the code. Suspense enforces this itself, not through the prompt, so it holds for Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode alike. The new tests pass; I haven't tried it with a real task in the app.

**How it works**
- **Snapshot and put back** (new `src/mode_guard.rs`): when a Code or Spec task starts, Suspense copies the location that mode can't touch. The locations come from `piton.config.pi`: `root` for the spec, `codeRoot` for the code. Every half second while the task runs, and once more when it ends, any change there is undone. Edited or deleted files are restored, and new files are removed. This also catches changes made through shell commands like `sed -i` or `>` redirects.
- **Claude Code is blocked up front:** its runs get a rule denying its file-editing tools anything under that location, so it's refused at once instead of having its work silently undone. Codex and OpenCode have no equivalent flag, so for them the put-back is the only guard.
- **The task shows what was undone:** if anything was put back, the task's output ends with an error-styled note listing the files.
- **Scope:** Chain, Ask and Freeform are unaffected. Each step of a Chain is still guarded by its own mode.

**Behaviours to know about**
- **Your own edits:** saves from Suspense's editor during a run are kept. Other changes you make to the guarded location while a task runs will be undone, such as creating or renaming files from the file tree or discarding changes in the git panel. Only the editor save is exempted so far; tell me if you want the others added.
- **Cancelled tasks:** their changes to the guarded location are undone too. The spec currently says a cancelled task's changes are left as they are, so this is a deliberate exception.
- **Ignored files:** files that `.gitignore` excludes aren't guarded, such as build output in `target/`. The `.suspense` folder is also exempt, so the task's history and understanding files can still be written.

**Tests:** I added tests for which location each mode protects, undoing a Code task's spec changes, undoing a Spec task's code changes while it runs, keeping editor saves, and the Claude deny rule. They all pass. The full suite has 4 failures that also happen without my changes (the code-to-spec and system-prompt defaults tests). A few more fail on and off only when everything runs at once; they failed the same way without my changes, and each passes when run by itself.

**Still to do**
- The spec doesn't describe any of this, and I couldn't update it from Code mode. The Modes and Sending specs in `spec/` need to cover it, including the cancelled-task exception; sending this task to Spec would do that.
- The working tree also has uncommitted changes in files I didn't touch (`main_window.rs`, `ribbon/`, `scrollbar.rs` and others). I left those alone.
